title: Common strict-tower models and descent for the two completed pullbacks
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. All schemes $W$ below are noetherian and finite dimensional with $\ell$ invertible, with the meaning and the common full integral constructible categories of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $R_{E,W}=\lim_{n\geq1}(A_{E,n})_W$ on the small pro-etale site, and use framework and PBC completed pullbacks $F^s_{h,E},F^p_{h,E}$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Write $I_{W,E}$ for restriction along the quotient-normalized coefficient identity, giving the integral identity equivalence. All equalities below use these fixed identity transports; we suppress $I$ when source and target already have the same module presentation. For a scheme isomorphism $h:U\simeq T$, let $G_{h,E}$ be ordinary derived module pullback on the completed rings. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ over $R_{E,T}$ set
$$Q_{h,E}(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*(P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}(A_{E,n})_T),\qquad H(Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Q)[-1],$$
with the actual quotient transitions and $s_Q((x_n)_n)=(t_nx_{n+1})_n$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].
The quotient-defined ring map $h^{-1}R_{E,T}\to R_{E,U}$ is an isomorphism, and $G_{h,E}$ is exact inverse image with this transported action. Both completed pullback constructions are realizations of the identical strict tower $Q_{h,E}(P)$, including every quotient transition: the framework realization is $H(Q)$ and the PBC realization is $R\lim Q$. With a K-injective tower resolution $q:Q\to I_\bullet$ with injective terms, the arrow
$$[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]:H(Q)\longrightarrow\lim I_\bullet,\qquad \iota_I(z)=(0,z),$$
is a natural isomorphism on ambient derived categories. It is independent of $P$, $q$ and common refinements under the canonical defining resolution comparisons, and natural for all derived morphisms. It restricts to a natural integral constructible isomorphism $b^{\rm int}_{h,E}:I_{U,E}F^s_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^p_{h,E}I_{T,E}$, with ambient lift $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E}$. These assertions concern entire strict towers, and impose no K-flatness over the completed ring on their individual quotient complexes.

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], $h^{-1}$ is an exact equivalence, preserves the coefficient limit, and its finite coefficient isomorphisms commute with every quotient homomorphism. Consequently the composite
$h^{-1}R_{E,T}\cong\lim_n h^{-1}(A_{E,n})_T\cong\lim_n(A_{E,n})_U=R_{E,U}$
is invertible. Its $n$-th projection is $c_{A_{E,n}}^h h^{-1}(\pi_{T,n})$, so it is precisely the quotient-defined structure map, by the uniqueness part of the limit. The same projection calculation gives compatibility with $A_{E,n+1}\to A_{E,n}$. Under the fixed identity transports $I_{W,E}$, the finite component $h^{-1}(A_{E,n})_T\to(A_{E,n})_U$ used by the coefficient map $c_h$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] is this same $c^h_{A_{E,n}}$, by the final clause of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]; hence the map above is also the PBC coefficient map $c_h$. By [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso], ordinary module pullback along this map is inverse image with transported action: the tensor map sends $m\otimes a$ to $c^{-1}(a)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. It is therefore exact. The exact-functor results [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identify its ordinary derived functor $G_{h,E}$ with this termwise functor on every ambient complex.

proof.text: Fix a flat-term K-flat $P$ representing $K$ and use all its reductions simultaneously. By [def-pur-integral-derived-operations, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] the framework functor is represented by $H(Q_{h,E}(P))$. This is its actual construction, not a selection of an object from a distinguished triangle. In particular the transition is the image of $1_P\otimes\rho_n$ under finite inverse image and restriction of scalars. At finite level the tensor description of module inverse image agrees with inverse image with transported action, by [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] for the ring-sheaf isomorphism $c^h_{A_{E,n}}$ of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], clause 3: $h^{-1}(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ maps to $b\,h^{-1}(x\otimes a)$, and the inverse inserts $1$. Both composites are identities by tensor balancing. Applying the transition before or after this map gives $b\,h^{-1}(x\otimes\rho_n(a))$ in either case, with the coefficient actions identified by step 1. Thus the framework model retains precisely the specified strict quotient transitions.

source.place: Final sentence: comparison of the two coefficient-category pullbacks, common strict quotient-tower computation

proof.text: The PBC reduction functor of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] is computed on the same $P$ by the strict tower $P_n=P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}(A_{E,n})_T$, restricted to $R_{E,T}$, with transition $1\otimes\rho_n$. Apply the module functor of step 1 levelwise to towers. This is exact since kernels and cokernels of towers are levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization, lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], its left derived functor is computed on EVERY tower complex by that exact levelwise functor. In particular, any resolving-class replacement used in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] maps by a quasi-isomorphism to the direct image of the displayed reduction tower. At level $n$ this direct image is canonically $\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*P_n$: multiplication identifies the transported module action, and the coefficient projection square in step 1 identifies the restricted completed-ring actions. The calculation in step 2 identifies each transition. Thus the whole PBC derived tower, including its canonical resolution comparison, is $Q_{h,E}(P)$, and its realization is $R\lim Q_{h,E}(P)$. No level of this tower is asserted K-flat over $R_{E,T}$ or $R_{E,U}$.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5), with the completed-ring strict-tower definition and exact-isomorphism specialization

proof.text:
Countable products of $R_{E,U}$-module sheaves on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] with this ring sheaf and with the entire strict tower $Q=Q_{h,E}(P)$. Its natural comparison is
$\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]:H(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim I_\bullet$,
where $q:Q\to I_\bullet$ is a K-injective tower resolution with injective terms and $\iota_I(z)=(0,z)$. The cited comparison states that both arrows of this zigzag are quasi-isomorphisms, fixes the zero shifted-product component, and states naturality in $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(R_{E,U})))$ and independence of resolution. Thus it supplies exactly the required normalized map between the realizations from steps 2 and 3.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; normalized functorial strict-cone refinement in lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison

proof.text:
Use the actual reduction functor into the derived category of strict towers supplied by [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], followed by the exact derived levelwise functor of step 3. This gives an ambient derived functor $B_{h,E}$ with canonical computation $B_{h,E}(K)\cong Q_{h,E}(P)$. The canonical framework computation comparisons are those of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]; the PBC comparisons are those in its definition, identified in step 3. Whiskering the natural isomorphism $\rho:H\Rightarrow R\lim$ of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] by $B_{h,E}$ therefore gives $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E}$. For a derived arrow $f:K\to L$ its naturality equation is
$R\lim(B_{h,E}f)\,\rho_{B_{h,E}K}=\rho_{B_{h,E}L}\,H(B_{h,E}f)$.
This equation holds for all derived arrows, not merely levelwise families. On a different representative or common refinement the two computation isomorphisms conjugate this same component of $\rho$; naturality gives equality after those specified comparisons. Independence of $q$ is already part of step 4. Hence neither choices of $P$ nor of tower resolutions add any further choice to the comparison.

proof.text:
By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], the framework completed pullback sends the full integral constructible category on $T$ into that on $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], these are the same full subcategories as the PBC categories under the fixed coefficient identity transports $I_{W,E}$. The ambient isomorphism from step 5 consequently places its PBC target in the same integral category as its framework source. Fullness restricts both $b^{\rm amb}_{h,E}$ and its inverse and restricts their naturality identities. Restoring the fixed transports gives
$b^{\rm int}_{h,E}:I_{U,E}F^s_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^p_{h,E}I_{T,E}$.
This restriction changes none of the strict-tower models or comparison maps; its ambient lift is the component already constructed. The assertions hold for each finite coefficient field $E$, without imposing any additional hypothesis on its quotient complexes.
